messages:
maya: Quick sync — we need a concise preflight/exit checklist for the upcoming release. Goal: unblock go/no-go by EOD Fri. Items I think must be explicit: SLA targets, docs & runbooks, oncall coverage, monitoring/alerts, and pricing/backstop. I'll paste a compact proposal below.

dan: +1. Can we keep SLA numbers minimal and realistic? We should avoid adding new SLOs that the runtime can't prove for 2 weeks.

maya: Agreed. Proposal (draft):
- SLA: 99.9% availability for hosted endpoints (90-day baseline), p95 latency < 400ms for short-text models, p99 < 1.2s for baseline traffic profile. Failure budget: 1% monthly.
- Docs: public API examples, migration notes for model variants, and an internal runbook for degraded modes and fallback rules.
- Support: rotation defined, escalation matrix with eng on-call + product owner, 2-hour initial response for Sev2+.
- Monitoring: synthetic smoke every minute, end-to-end traces for 99th percentile errors, and alert thresholds tied to failure budget burn.
- Pricing: staging pricing page, clear quota/burst policy, and support for emergency credit adjustments.

aaron: Hit on monitoring: synthetic every 60s is fine but add regional synths (us/eur) and a KV-cache hit-rate metric to watch. Also suggest automatic fallback to cheaper model on >= 70% CPU sustained for 3m.

sasha: Support notes: I can draft the customer-facing FAQ for common error modes (rate limit, degraded model, auth). For oncall, we need a runbook link and a single Slack shortcut to trigger page-notifications.

olivia: I'll own docs + runbook. ETA: first pass by Wed EOD. Will include the runbook checklist: reproduce, impact, rollback step, escalation contacts, communication template.

dan: SLA math question — failure budget 1% monthly seems high for prod. Can we express it as monthly error budget in minutes? Also we need a test harness that runs load samples to validate p95 numbers before GA.

maya: Good call. Let's convert: 1% monthly -> ~7.2 hours of downtime. We'll present both absolute minutes and percentage on the SLA doc. For validation, engineering should provide a 2-day load report on canary traffic.

aaron: I'll schedule canary jobs and add a grafana dashboard with the canary job and KV-cache panel. Also will wire alerts: failure-budget burn > 25%/24h and >50%/4h.

sasha: For support handoff, propose a 1-week overlap where SRE/serving team sits on support queue during rollout. That should smooth initial incidents.

maya: Decision items for EOD Fri: (1) Approve SLA numbers (percent + minutes), (2) Docs PR in flight, (3) Oncall handoff plan confirmed, (4) Canary load report scheduled, (5) Pricing/backstop note published. If any owner cannot meet ETA, say so now.

olivia: I can commit to docs PR by Wed; will add runbook link to this thread when ready.

dan: Engineering can produce canary load report by Thu. SLA numbers: let's tighten p99 target to 1.0s if canary looks good; keep 1.2s as fallback.

aaron: Oncall overlap: SRE can do Wed-Fri overlap window. I'll create rotation and the Slack shortcut.

sasha: I'll draft the customer FAQ and support escalation doc by Thu.

release-bot: Deployment plan created: https://internal/release/2243 — includes canary stages and abort criteria.

maya: Great — thanks everyone. Last ask: please drop the PR/link into this thread when you have it so gatekeepers can verify before the Friday decision. :thumbsup:
